# pr-1709: feat(1704): Codex/ChatGPT credential export + CI refresh action + provider queue support

## Description

Closes #1704 (AC5 owner-side, see below)

## Goal

Copilot-export parity for the Codex/ChatGPT credential: one command mints a fresh Bearer for headless/CI use, a GitHub workflow mints tokens from a stored refresh token (no browser after one-time login), and `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex` first-class.

## What changed

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);
  2. new `refreshTokenEnv:` field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation (lazy: chain build touches no network), memoized in memory, real mint = the existing `refreshChatGptCredentials` rotation-tolerant path; wrong-kind `refreshTokenEnv` is a hard parse error;
  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** — export command against a stored login: unit tests with fake store + injected refresh, no network (`test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart`, 9 tests).
- [x] **AC2** — import reads a fixture auth.json and lands the same slot shape; round-trips with the runtime (`ChatGptOAuthCredentials.decode` on the stored blob + expiry from `exp`): 4 tests in `test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart`.
- [x] **AC3** — the action mints from a refresh-token secret; `invalid_grant` fails fast and loudly (static action, exercised by CI on first use; the curl contract mirrors `_tokenRequest`).
- [x] **AC4** — queue failover tests: default-slot resolution, login-hint skip, mint-once/memoize, mint-failure error event, missing-refresh-env skip, wrong-kind hard error, raw-bearer passthrough, mint entry fails over like any other (8 tests in `providers_queue_test.dart` + 3 adapter tests in `chatgpt_codex_test.dart`). NO network anywhere in tests.
- [ ] **AC5** — one live smoke bench on chatgpt-codex through the action/queue + quota note: **OWNER-side** — needs real ChatGPT credentials (a real refresh-token secret and an account-backed run); this lane has no real creds. Everything short of the live run is in place and tested.
- [x] **AC6** — docs (README chatgpt section: export/import/CI action/queue examples) + CHANGELOG Unreleased line. Secrets never appear in logs/JSONL: the export prints only the access token (the minted credential — the point of the command), the refresh token never leaves the store and is asserted absent in every output test; queue notices name env NAMES only (`renderProviderQueueRows` contract unchanged); mint failures carry the provider error body, never the refresh token.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree — analyze + targeted suites)

- `dart analyze` on all 16 touched files: **No issues found** (after `dart format`).
- `dart test test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart` → **+139, all passed**.
- Regression guards green: `providers_queue_editor_test`, `settings_flow_providers_queue_test`, `providers_queue_rows_golden_test`, `agent_cli_queue_model_resync_test`, `quota_feed_test`, `cli_args_test`, `cli_help_test`, `purity_js_test`, `bin_main_wiring_reg_test`.

## Secrets-never-logged

Refresh tokens: never printed by the export (`--check` or not — asserted per test), never persisted by the queue lane, never in mint-failure messages. The action keeps the refresh token in a step env var and writes only the minted access token to `$GITHUB_ENV`. Redaction layers unchanged and upstream of every new surface.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1709
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1709
- **Title**: feat(1704): Codex/ChatGPT credential export + CI refresh action + provider queue support
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1704-codex-credential-export` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1813
- **Deletions**: -423
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z

## PR Description

Closes #1704 (AC5 owner-side, see below)

## Goal

Copilot-export parity for the Codex/ChatGPT credential: one command mints a fresh Bearer for headless/CI use, a GitHub workflow mints tokens from a stored refresh token (no browser after one-time login), and `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex` first-class.

## What changed

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);
  2. new `refreshTokenEnv:` field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation (lazy: chain build touches no network), memoized in memory, real mint = the existing `refreshChatGptCredentials` rotation-tolerant path; wrong-kind `refreshTokenEnv` is a hard parse error;
  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** — export command against a stored login: unit tests with fake store + injected refresh, no network (`test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart`, 9 tests).
- [x] **AC2** — import reads a fixture auth.json and lands the same slot shape; round-trips with the runtime (`ChatGptOAuthCredentials.decode` on the stored blob + expiry from `exp`): 4 tests in `test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart`.
- [x] **AC3** — the action mints from a refresh-token secret; `invalid_grant` fails fast and loudly (static action, exercised by CI on first use; the curl contract mirrors `_tokenRequest`).
- [x] **AC4** — queue failover tests: default-slot resolution, login-hint skip, mint-once/memoize, mint-failure error event, missing-refresh-env skip, wrong-kind hard error, raw-bearer passthrough, mint entry fails over like any other (8 tests in `providers_queue_test.dart` + 3 adapter tests in `chatgpt_codex_test.dart`). NO network anywhere in tests.
- [ ] **AC5** — one live smoke bench on chatgpt-codex through the action/queue + quota note: **OWNER-side** — needs real ChatGPT credentials (a real refresh-token secret and an account-backed run); this lane has no real creds. Everything short of the live run is in place and tested.
- [x] **AC6** — docs (README chatgpt section: export/import/CI action/queue examples) + CHANGELOG Unreleased line. Secrets never appear in logs/JSONL: the export prints only the access token (the minted credential — the point of the command), the refresh token never leaves the store and is asserted absent in every output test; queue notices name env NAMES only (`renderProviderQueueRows` contract unchanged); mint failures carry the provider error body, never the refresh token.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree — analyze + targeted suites)

- `dart analyze` on all 16 touched files: **No issues found** (after `dart format`).
- `dart test test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart` → **+139, all passed**.
- Regression guards green: `providers_queue_editor_test`, `settings_flow_providers_queue_test`, `providers_queue_rows_golden_test`, `agent_cli_queue_model_resync_test`, `quota_feed_test`, `cli_args_test`, `cli_help_test`, `purity_js_test`, `bin_main_wiring_reg_test`.

## Secrets-never-logged

Refresh tokens: never printed by the export (`--check` or not — asserted per test), never persisted by the queue lane, never in mint-failure messages. The action keeps the refresh token in a step env var and writes only the minted access token to `$GITHUB_ENV`. Redaction layers unchanged and upstream of every new surface.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1709
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1709
- **Title**: feat(1704): Codex/ChatGPT credential export + CI refresh action + provider queue support
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1704-codex-credential-export` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1813
- **Deletions**: -423
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z

## PR Description

Closes #1704 (AC5 owner-side, see below)

## Goal

Copilot-export parity for the Codex/ChatGPT credential: one command mints a fresh Bearer for headless/CI use, a GitHub workflow mints tokens from a stored refresh token (no browser after one-time login), and `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex` first-class.

## What changed

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);
  2. new `refreshTokenEnv:` field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation (lazy: chain build touches no network), memoized in memory, real mint = the existing `refreshChatGptCredentials` rotation-tolerant path; wrong-kind `refreshTokenEnv` is a hard parse error;
  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** — export command against a stored login: unit tests with fake store + injected refresh, no network (`test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart`, 9 tests).
- [x] **AC2** — import reads a fixture auth.json and lands the same slot shape; round-trips with the runtime (`ChatGptOAuthCredentials.decode` on the stored blob + expiry from `exp`): 4 tests in `test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart`.
- [x] **AC3** — the action mints from a refresh-token secret; `invalid_grant` fails fast and loudly (static action, exercised by CI on first use; the curl contract mirrors `_tokenRequest`).
- [x] **AC4** — queue failover tests: default-slot resolution, login-hint skip, mint-once/memoize, mint-failure error event, missing-refresh-env skip, wrong-kind hard error, raw-bearer passthrough, mint entry fails over like any other (8 tests in `providers_queue_test.dart` + 3 adapter tests in `chatgpt_codex_test.dart`). NO network anywhere in tests.
- [ ] **AC5** — one live smoke bench on chatgpt-codex through the action/queue + quota note: **OWNER-side** — needs real ChatGPT credentials (a real refresh-token secret and an account-backed run); this lane has no real creds. Everything short of the live run is in place and tested.
- [x] **AC6** — docs (README chatgpt section: export/import/CI action/queue examples) + CHANGELOG Unreleased line. Secrets never appear in logs/JSONL: the export prints only the access token (the minted credential — the point of the command), the refresh token never leaves the store and is asserted absent in every output test; queue notices name env NAMES only (`renderProviderQueueRows` contract unchanged); mint failures carry the provider error body, never the refresh token.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree — analyze + targeted suites)

- `dart analyze` on all 16 touched files: **No issues found** (after `dart format`).
- `dart test test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart` → **+139, all passed**.
- Regression guards green: `providers_queue_editor_test`, `settings_flow_providers_queue_test`, `providers_queue_rows_golden_test`, `agent_cli_queue_model_resync_test`, `quota_feed_test`, `cli_args_test`, `cli_help_test`, `purity_js_test`, `bin_main_wiring_reg_test`.

## Secrets-never-logged

Refresh tokens: never printed by the export (`--check` or not — asserted per test), never persisted by the queue lane, never in mint-failure messages. The action keeps the refresh token in a step env var and writes only the minted access token to `$GITHUB_ENV`. Redaction layers unchanged and upstream of every new surface.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1709
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1709
- **Title**: feat(1704): Codex/ChatGPT credential export + CI refresh action + provider queue support
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1704-codex-credential-export` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1813
- **Deletions**: -423
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z

## PR Description

Closes #1704 (AC5 owner-side, see below)

## Goal

Copilot-export parity for the Codex/ChatGPT credential: one command mints a fresh Bearer for headless/CI use, a GitHub workflow mints tokens from a stored refresh token (no browser after one-time login), and `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex` first-class.

## What changed

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);
  2. new `refreshTokenEnv:` field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation (lazy: chain build touches no network), memoized in memory, real mint = the existing `refreshChatGptCredentials` rotation-tolerant path; wrong-kind `refreshTokenEnv` is a hard parse error;
  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** — export command against a stored login: unit tests with fake store + injected refresh, no network (`test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart`, 9 tests).
- [x] **AC2** — import reads a fixture auth.json and lands the same slot shape; round-trips with the runtime (`ChatGptOAuthCredentials.decode` on the stored blob + expiry from `exp`): 4 tests in `test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart`.
- [x] **AC3** — the action mints from a refresh-token secret; `invalid_grant` fails fast and loudly (static action, exercised by CI on first use; the curl contract mirrors `_tokenRequest`).
- [x] **AC4** — queue failover tests: default-slot resolution, login-hint skip, mint-once/memoize, mint-failure error event, missing-refresh-env skip, wrong-kind hard error, raw-bearer passthrough, mint entry fails over like any other (8 tests in `providers_queue_test.dart` + 3 adapter tests in `chatgpt_codex_test.dart`). NO network anywhere in tests.
- [ ] **AC5** — one live smoke bench on chatgpt-codex through the action/queue + quota note: **OWNER-side** — needs real ChatGPT credentials (a real refresh-token secret and an account-backed run); this lane has no real creds. Everything short of the live run is in place and tested.
- [x] **AC6** — docs (README chatgpt section: export/import/CI action/queue examples) + CHANGELOG Unreleased line. Secrets never appear in logs/JSONL: the export prints only the access token (the minted credential — the point of the command), the refresh token never leaves the store and is asserted absent in every output test; queue notices name env NAMES only (`renderProviderQueueRows` contract unchanged); mint failures carry the provider error body, never the refresh token.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree — analyze + targeted suites)

- `dart analyze` on all 16 touched files: **No issues found** (after `dart format`).
- `dart test test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart` → **+139, all passed**.
- Regression guards green: `providers_queue_editor_test`, `settings_flow_providers_queue_test`, `providers_queue_rows_golden_test`, `agent_cli_queue_model_resync_test`, `quota_feed_test`, `cli_args_test`, `cli_help_test`, `purity_js_test`, `bin_main_wiring_reg_test`.

## Secrets-never-logged

Refresh tokens: never printed by the export (`--check` or not — asserted per test), never persisted by the queue lane, never in mint-failure messages. The action keeps the refresh token in a step env var and writes only the minted access token to `$GITHUB_ENV`. Redaction layers unchanged and upstream of every new surface.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1709
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1709
- **Title**: feat(1704): Codex/ChatGPT credential export + CI refresh action + provider queue support
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1704-codex-credential-export` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1813
- **Deletions**: -423
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z

## PR Description

Closes #1704 (AC5 owner-side, see below)

## Goal

Copilot-export parity for the Codex/ChatGPT credential: one command mints a fresh Bearer for headless/CI use, a GitHub workflow mints tokens from a stored refresh token (no browser after one-time login), and `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex` first-class.

## What changed

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);
  2. new `refreshTokenEnv:` field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation (lazy: chain build touches no network), memoized in memory, real mint = the existing `refreshChatGptCredentials` rotation-tolerant path; wrong-kind `refreshTokenEnv` is a hard parse error;
  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

## Acceptance criteria

# pr-1709: feat(1704): Codex/ChatGPT credential export + CI refresh action + provider queue support

## Description

Closes #1704 (AC5 owner-side, see below)

## Goal

Copilot-export parity for the Codex/ChatGPT credential: one command mints a fresh Bearer for headless/CI use, a GitHub workflow mints tokens from a stored refresh token (no browser after one-time login), and `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex` first-class.

## What changed

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);

  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1709
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1709
- **Title**: feat(1704): Codex/ChatGPT credential export + CI refresh action + provider queue support
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1704-codex-credential-export` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1813
- **Deletions**: -423
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z

## PR Description

Closes #1704 (AC5 owner-side, see below)

## Goal

Copilot-export parity for the Codex/ChatGPT credential: one command mints a fresh Bearer for headless/CI use, a GitHub workflow mints tokens from a stored refresh token (no browser after one-time login), and `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex` first-class.

## What changed

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);
  2. new `refreshTokenEnv:` field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation (lazy: chain build touches no network), memoized in memory, real mint = the existing `refreshChatGptCredentials` rotation-tolerant path; wrong-kind `refreshTokenEnv` is a hard parse error;
  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** — export command against a stored login: unit tests with fake store + injected refresh, no network (`test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart`, 9 tests).
- [x] **AC2** — import reads a fixture auth.json and lands the same slot shape; round-trips with the runtime (`ChatGptOAuthCredentials.decode` on the stored blob + expiry from `exp`): 4 tests in `test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart`.
- [x] **AC3** — the action mints from a refresh-token secret; `invalid_grant` fails fast and loudly (static action, exercised by CI on first use; the curl contract mirrors `_tokenRequest`).
- [x] **AC4** — queue failover tests: default-slot resolution, login-hint skip, mint-once/memoize, mint-failure error event, missing-refresh-env skip, wrong-kind hard error, raw-bearer passthrough, mint entry fails over like any other (8 tests in `providers_queue_test.dart` + 3 adapter tests in `chatgpt_codex_test.dart`). NO network anywhere in tests.
- [ ] **AC5** — one live smoke bench on chatgpt-codex through the action/queue + quota note: **OWNER-side** — needs real ChatGPT credentials (a real refresh-token secret and an account-backed run); this lane has no real creds. Everything short of the live run is in place and tested.
- [x] **AC6** — docs (README chatgpt section: export/import/CI action/queue examples) + CHANGELOG Unreleased line. Secrets never appear in logs/JSONL: the export prints only the access token (the minted credential — the point of the command), the refresh token never leaves the store and is asserted absent in every output test; queue notices name env NAMES only (`renderProviderQueueRows` contract unchanged); mint failures carry the provider error body, never the refresh token.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree — analyze + targeted suites)

- `dart analyze` on all 16 touched files: **No issues found** (after `dart format`).
- `dart test test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart` → **+139, all passed**.
- Regression guards green: `providers_queue_editor_test`, `settings_flow_providers_queue_test`, `providers_queue_rows_golden_test`, `agent_cli_queue_model_resync_test`, `quota_feed_test`, `cli_args_test`, `cli_help_test`, `purity_js_test`, `bin_main_wiring_reg_test`.

## Secrets-never-logged

Refresh tokens: never printed by the export (`--check` or not — asserted per test), never persisted by the queue lane, never in mint-failure messages. The action keeps the refresh token in a step env var and writes only the minted access token to `$GITHUB_ENV`. Redaction layers unchanged and upstream of every new surface.

+/// Headless `fa provider export <name> [--check]` (issue #1704): mints a
+/// fresh Bearer credential for the saved ChatGPT/Codex login and prints the
+/// shell lines external tools eval — the `GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)`
+/// parity for the Codex backend.
+///
+/// The full OAuth blob lives in the entry's secure-store slot; the export
+/// refreshes it when stale (so the minted access token is fresh, not the
+/// possibly-expired stored one) and prints ONLY the access token — the
+/// refresh token never leaves the store. `--check` reports credential
+/// health without printing any secret. The base URL is always the Codex
+/// backend: ChatGPT access tokens are accepted ONLY by
+/// `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/...`, never by api.openai.com.
+library;
+
+import '../exceptions.dart';
+import '../model_roles/provider_catalog.dart' show resolveCliProviderSpec;
+import '../providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart';
+import 'agent_cli.dart';
+import 'cli_args.dart';
+import 'custom_providers.dart';
+
+/// The exported base URL: the one endpoint family these tokens serve.
+const chatGptExportBaseUrl = chatGptCodexBaseUrl;
+
+/// The shell lines an external tool evals: `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>`
+/// + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=<codex backend>`.
+String chatGptExportLines({required String accessToken}) =>
+    'export OPENAI_API_KEY=$accessToken\n'
+    'export OPENAI_BASE_URL=$chatGptExportBaseUrl';
+
+/// The `--check` health lines for [credentials]: expiry state and
+/// refreshability, never a token value. The SSO caveat is part of the
+/// contract (issue #1704 notes): corporate session policies can shorten
+/// lifetimes or revoke refresh tokens, so the check says exactly that.
+List<String> chatGptExportCheckLines(
+  ChatGptOAuthCredentials credentials,
+  String name,
+  DateTime now,
+) {
+  final expiresAt = credentials.expiresAt;
+  final expiry = expiresAt == null
+      ? 'access token expiry unknown'
+      : expiresAt.isBefore(now)
+      ? 'access token EXPIRED'
+      : 'access token expires in ${expiresAt.difference(now).inMinutes} min';
+  return [
+    // The decode contract guarantees a non-empty refresh token, so a
+    // stored login is always refreshable HERE — the risk is revocation.
+    '$name: $expiry; refresh token present (refreshable)',
+    'note: corporate/SSO session policies can shorten lifetimes or revoke '
+        'refresh tokens at any time',
+  ];
+}
+
+/// Resolves the saved ChatGPT entry for [name]: the registry's own lookup
+/// (case-insensitive, alias spellings), narrowed to `chatgpt-codex`-kind
+/// entries. Null when no saved login of that kind matches.
+CustomProviderEntry? findChatGptExportEntry(
+  List<CustomProviderEntry> entries,
+  String name,
+) {
+  final spec = resolveCliProviderSpec(name);
+  if (spec?.kind == 'chatgpt-codex') {
+    // The kind itself (`chatgpt` / `chatgpt-codex`): the saved entry is
+    // located by its apiType, first match.
+    for (final entry in entries) {
+      if (resolveCliProviderSpec(entry.apiType)?.kind == 'chatgpt-codex') {
+        return entry;
+      }
+    }
+    return null;

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1709
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1709
- **Title**: feat(1704): Codex/ChatGPT credential export + CI refresh action + provider queue support
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1704-codex-credential-export` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1813
- **Deletions**: -423
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z

## PR Description

Closes #1704 (AC5 owner-side, see below)

## Goal

Copilot-export parity for the Codex/ChatGPT credential: one command mints a fresh Bearer for headless/CI use, a GitHub workflow mints tokens from a stored refresh token (no browser after one-time login), and `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex` first-class.

## What changed

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);
  2. new `refreshTokenEnv:` field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation (lazy: chain build touches no network), memoized in memory, real mint = the existing `refreshChatGptCredentials` rotation-tolerant path; wrong-kind `refreshTokenEnv` is a hard parse error;
  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

## Acceptance criteria

# pr-1709: feat(1704): Codex/ChatGPT credential export + CI refresh action + provider queue support

## Description

Closes #1704 (AC5 owner-side, see below)

## Goal

Copilot-export parity for the Codex/ChatGPT credential: one command mints a fresh Bearer for headless/CI use, a GitHub workflow mints tokens from a stored refresh token (no browser after one-time login), and `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex` first-class.

## What changed

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);
  2. new `refreshTokenEnv:` field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation (lazy: chain build touches no network), memoized in memory, real mint = the existing `refreshChatGptCredentials` rotation-tolerant path; wrong-kind `refreshTokenEnv` is a hard parse error;
  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

- [x] **AC3** — the action mints from a refresh-token secret; `invalid_grant` fails fast and loudly (static action, exercised by CI on first use; the curl contract mirrors `_tokenRequest`).
- [x] **AC4** — queue failover tests: default-slot resolution, login-hint skip, mint-once/memoize, mint-failure error event, missing-refresh-env skip, wrong-kind hard error, raw-bearer passthrough, mint entry fails over like any other (8 tests in `providers_queue_test.dart` + 3 adapter tests in `chatgpt_codex_test.dart`). NO network anywhere in tests.

- [x] **AC6** — docs (README chatgpt section: export/import/CI action/queue examples) + CHANGELOG Unreleased line. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1709
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1709
- **Title**: feat(1704): Codex/ChatGPT credential export + CI refresh action + provider queue support
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1704-codex-credential-export` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1813
- **Deletions**: -423
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z

## PR Description

Closes #1704 (AC5 owner-side, see below)

## Goal

Copilot-export parity for the Codex/ChatGPT credential: one command mints a fresh Bearer for headless/CI use, a GitHub workflow mints tokens from a stored refresh token (no browser after one-time login), and `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex` first-class.

## What changed

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);
  2. new `refreshTokenEnv:` field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation (lazy: chain build touches no network), memoized in memory, real mint = the existing `refreshChatGptCredentials` rotation-tolerant path; wrong-kind `refreshTokenEnv` is a hard parse error;
  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** — export command against a stored login: unit tests with fake store + injected refresh, no network (`test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart`, 9 tests).
- [x] **AC2** — import reads a fixture auth.json and lands the same slot shape; round-trips with the runtime (`ChatGptOAuthCredentials.decode` on the stored blob + expiry from `exp`): 4 tests in `test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart`.
- [x] **AC3** — the action mints from a refresh-token secret; `invalid_grant` fails fast and loudly (static action, exercised by CI on first use; the curl contract mirrors `_tokenRequest`).
- [x] **AC4** — queue failover tests: default-slot resolution, login-hint skip, mint-once/memoize, mint-failure error event, missing-refresh-env skip, wrong-kind hard error, raw-bearer passthrough, mint entry fails over like any other (8 tests in `providers_queue_test.dart` + 3 adapter tests in `chatgpt_codex_test.dart`). NO network anywhere in tests.
- [ ] **AC5** — one live smoke bench on chatgpt-codex through the action/queue + quota note: **OWNER-side** — needs real ChatGPT credentials (a real refresh-token secret and an account-backed run); this lane has no real creds. Everything short of the live run is in place and tested.
- [x] **AC6** — docs (README chatgpt section: export/import/CI action/queue examples) + CHANGELOG Unreleased line. Secrets never appear in logs/JSONL: the export prints only the access token (the minted credential — the point of the command), the refresh token never leaves the store and is asserted absent in every output test; queue notices name env NAMES only (`renderProviderQueueRows` contract unchanged); mint failures carry the provider error body, never the refresh token.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree — analyze + targeted suites)

- `dart analyze` on all 16 touched files: **No issues found** (after `dart format`).
- `dart test test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart` → **+139, all passed**.
- Regression guards green: `providers_queue_editor_test`, `settings_flow_providers_queue_test`, `providers_queue_rows_golden_test`, `agent_cli_queue_model_resync_test`, `quota_feed_test`, `cli_args_test`, `cli_help_test`, `purity_js_test`, `bin_main_wiring_reg_test`.

## Secrets-never-logged

Refresh tokens: never printed by the export (`--check` or not — asserted per test), never persisted by the queue lane, never in mint-failure messages. The action keeps the refresh token in a step env var and writes only the minted access token to `$GITHUB_ENV`. Redaction layers unchanged and upstream of every new surface.

+/// Headless `fa provider export <name> [--check]` (issue #1704): mints a
+/// fresh Bearer credential for the saved ChatGPT/Codex login and prints the
+/// shell lines external tools eval — the `GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)`
+/// parity for the Codex backend.
+///
+/// The full OAuth blob lives in the entry's secure-store slot; the export
+/// refreshes it when stale (so the minted access token is fresh, not the
+/// possibly-expired stored one) and prints ONLY the access token — the
+/// refresh token never leaves the store. `--check` reports credential
+/// health without printing any secret. The base URL is always the Codex
+/// backend: ChatGPT access tokens are accepted ONLY by
+/// `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/...`, never by api.openai.com.
+library;
+
+import '../exceptions.dart';
+import '../model_roles/provider_catalog.dart' show resolveCliProviderSpec;
+import '../providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart';
+import 'agent_cli.dart';
+import 'cli_args.dart';
+import 'custom_providers.dart';

+/// The exported base URL: the one endpoint family these tokens serve.
+const chatGptExportBaseUrl = chatGptCodexBaseUrl;
+
+/// The shell lines an external tool evals: `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>`
+/// + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=<codex backend>`.
+String chatGptExportLines({required String accessToken}) =>
+    'export OPENAI_API_KEY=$accessToken\n'
+    'export OPENAI_BASE_URL=$chatGptExportBaseUrl';
+
+/// The `--check` health lines for [credentials]: expiry state and
+/// refreshability, never a token value. The SSO caveat is part of the
+/// contract (issue #1704 notes): corporate session policies can shorten
+/// lifetimes or revoke refresh tokens, so the check says exactly that.
+List<String> chatGptExportCheckLines(
+  ChatGptOAuthCredentials credentials,
+  String name,
+  DateTime now,
+) {
+  final expiresAt = credentials.expiresAt;
+  final expiry = expiresAt == null
+      ? 'access token expiry unknown'
+      : expiresAt.isBefore(now)
+      ? 'access token EXPIRED'
+      : 'access token expires in ${expiresAt.difference(now).inMinutes} min';

+    // stored login is always refreshable HERE — the risk is revocation.
+    '$name: $expiry; refresh token present (refreshable)',
+    'note: corporate/SSO session policies can shorten lifetimes or revoke '
+        'refresh tokens at any time',

+  String name,

Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1709
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1709
- **Title**: feat(1704): Codex/ChatGPT credential export + CI refresh action + provider queue support
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1704-codex-credential-export` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 19
- **Additions**: +1813
- **Deletions**: -423
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:49:42Z

## PR Description

Closes #1704 (AC5 owner-side, see below)

## Goal

Copilot-export parity for the Codex/ChatGPT credential: one command mints a fresh Bearer for headless/CI use, a GitHub workflow mints tokens from a stored refresh token (no browser after one-time login), and `providersQueue:` entries speak `chatgpt-codex` first-class.

## What changed

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);
  2. new `refreshTokenEnv:` field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation (lazy: chain build touches no network), memoized in memory, real mint = the existing `refreshChatGptCredentials` rotation-tolerant path; wrong-kind `refreshTokenEnv` is a hard parse error;
  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** — export command against a stored login: unit tests with fake store + injected refresh, no network (`test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart`, 9 tests).
- [x] **AC2** — import reads a fixture auth.json and lands the same slot shape; round-trips with the runtime (`ChatGptOAuthCredentials.decode` on the stored blob + expiry from `exp`): 4 tests in `test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart`.
- [x] **AC3** — the action mints from a refresh-token secret; `invalid_grant` fails fast and loudly (static action, exercised by CI on first use; the curl contract mirrors `_tokenRequest`).
- [x] **AC4** — queue failover tests: default-slot resolution, login-hint skip, mint-once/memoize, mint-failure error event, missing-refresh-env skip, wrong-kind hard error, raw-bearer passthrough, mint entry fails over like any other (8 tests in `providers_queue_test.dart` + 3 adapter tests in `chatgpt_codex_test.dart`). NO network anywhere in tests.
- [ ] **AC5** — one live smoke bench on chatgpt-codex through the action/queue + quota note: **OWNER-side** — needs real ChatGPT credentials (a real refresh-token secret and an account-backed run); this lane has no real creds. Everything short of the live run is in place and tested.
- [x] **AC6** — docs (README chatgpt section: export/import/CI action/queue examples) + CHANGELOG Unreleased line. Secrets never appear in logs/JSONL: the export prints only the access token (the minted credential — the point of the command), the refresh token never leaves the store and is asserted absent in every output test; queue notices name env NAMES only (`renderProviderQueueRows` contract unchanged); mint failures carry the provider error body, never the refresh token.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree — analyze + targeted suites)

- `dart analyze` on all 16 touched files: **No issues found** (after `dart format`).
- `dart test test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart` → **+139, all passed**.
- Regression guards green: `providers_queue_editor_test`, `settings_flow_providers_queue_test`, `providers_queue_rows_golden_test`, `agent_cli_queue_model_resync_test`, `quota_feed_test`, `cli_args_test`, `cli_help_test`, `purity_js_test`, `bin_main_wiring_reg_test`.

## Secrets-never-logged

Refresh tokens: never printed by the export (`--check` or not — asserted per test), never persisted by the queue lane, never in mint-failure messages. The action keeps the refresh token in a step env var and writes only the minted access token to `$GITHUB_ENV`. Redaction layers unchanged and upstream of every new surface.

+/// refreshes it when stale (so the minted access token is fresh, not the
+/// possibly-expired stored one) and prints ONLY the access token — the
+/// refresh token never leaves the store. `--check` reports credential
+/// health without printing any secret. The base URL is always the Codex
+/// backend: ChatGPT access tokens are accepted ONLY by
+/// `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/...`, never by api.openai.com.
+library;

+import '../model_roles/provider_catalog.dart' show resolveCliProviderSpec;

+import 'agent_cli.dart';

+/// + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=<codex backend>`.
+String chatGptExportLines({required String accessToken}) =>
+    'export OPENAI_API_KEY=$accessToken\n'
+    'export OPENAI_BASE_URL=$chatGptExportBaseUrl';
+
+/// The `--check` health lines for [credentials]: expiry state and
+/// refreshability, never a token value. The SSO caveat is part of the
+/// contract (issue #1704 notes): corporate session policies can shorten
+/// lifetimes or revoke refresh tokens, so the check says exactly that.
+List<String> chatGptExportCheckLines(
+  ChatGptOAuthCredentials credentials,
+  String name,
+  DateTime now,
+) {
+  final expiresAt = credentials.expiresAt;
+  final expiry = expiresAt == null
+      ? 'access token expiry unknown'
+      : expiresAt.isBefore(now)
+      ? 'access token EXPIRED'
+      : 'access token expires in ${expiresAt.difference(now).inMinutes} min';

+    // stored login is always refreshable HERE — the risk is revocation.
+    '$name: $expiry; refresh token present (refreshable)',
+    'note: corporate/SSO session policies can shorten lifetimes or revoke '
+        'refresh tokens at any time',

Does not block merge. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. ## Goal

- **`fa provider export <name> [--check]`** — resolves the saved ChatGPT login's OAuth blob from its secure-store slot (entry `keyName`, then the legacy `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` slot), refreshes when stale, prints `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>` + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` (never api.openai.com — these tokens serve only the Codex backend). `--check` reports health with the SSO caveat, zero secrets. New `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_credential_export.dart`, routed like `fa config export-providers` (cli_args subcommand + bin interception).
- **`/provider chatgpt import [path]`** — reads a `codex login` session (`~/.codex/auth.json`, schema `{"tokens": {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account_id}, "last_refresh"}`) and applies it through the SAME storage/registry/switch path as the OAuth flow (name prompt, per-account Keychain slot, model pick). Expiry comes from the access token's own `exp` claim (`jwtExpClaim` — the one JWT payload reader `jwtPayloadClaims` now shared by the email/account-id/exp readers). Parser: `parseCodexAuthJson` in chatgpt_oauth.dart.
- **`.github/actions/chatgpt-codex-auth`** — composite action; direct `curl` against `auth.openai.com/oauth/token` with the codex client id, no third-party action. `invalid_grant`/`invalid_request` fails the job with a `::error::` naming the re-auth + secret-update path; other non-200s fail with the body. Exports `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **Provider Queue** (`providersQueue:` / `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) — `chatgpt-codex` entries resolve credentials on a ladder:
  1. `apiKeyEnv` value (full OAuth blob **or** a plain Bearer token — `streamChatGptCodex` no longer throws `FormatException: OAuth credentials are not an object`; raw bearer rides as-is, refresh degrades, a 401 surfaces as the auth death the queue fails over on; a partial JSON object degrades to its own `access_token`);
  2. new `refreshTokenEnv:` field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation (lazy: chain build touches no network), memoized in memory, real mint = the existing `refreshChatGptCredentials` rotation-tolerant path; wrong-kind `refreshTokenEnv` is a hard parse error;
  3. `apiKeyEnv` omitted → the default Keychain slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name (saved-login slot auto-resolve; `{"ref": ...}` entries keep materializing their entry's own keyName). Refresh stays in-memory: the queue lane never writes the Keychain back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** — export command against a stored login: unit tests with fake store + injected refresh, no network (`test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart`, 9 tests).
- [x] **AC2** — import reads a fixture auth.json and lands the same slot shape; round-trips with the runtime (`ChatGptOAuthCredentials.decode` on the stored blob + expiry from `exp`): 4 tests in `test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart`.
- [x] **AC3** — the action mints from a refresh-token secret; `invalid_grant` fails fast and loudly (static action, exercised by CI on first use; the curl contract mirrors `_tokenRequest`).
- [x] **AC4** — queue failover tests: default-slot resolution, login-hint skip, mint-once/memoize, mint-failure error event, missing-refresh-env skip, wrong-kind hard error, raw-bearer passthrough, mint entry fails over like any other (8 tests in `providers_queue_test.dart` + 3 adapter tests in `chatgpt_codex_test.dart`). NO network anywhere in tests.
- [ ] **AC5** — one live smoke bench on chatgpt-codex through the action/queue + quota note: **OWNER-side** — needs real ChatGPT credentials (a real refresh-token secret and an account-backed run); this lane has no real creds. Everything short of the live run is in place and tested.
- [x] **AC6** — docs (README chatgpt section: export/import/CI action/queue examples) + CHANGELOG Unreleased line. Secrets never appear in logs/JSONL: the export prints only the access token (the minted credential — the point of the command), the refresh token never leaves the store and is asserted absent in every output test; queue notices name env NAMES only (`renderProviderQueueRows` contract unchanged); mint failures carry the provider error body, never the refresh token.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree — analyze + targeted suites)

- `dart analyze` on all 16 touched files: **No issues found** (after `dart format`).
- `dart test test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_credential_export_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart` → **+139, all passed**.
- Regression guards green: `providers_queue_editor_test`, `settings_flow_providers_queue_test`, `providers_queue_rows_golden_test`, `agent_cli_queue_model_resync_test`, `quota_feed_test`, `cli_args_test`, `cli_help_test`, `purity_js_test`, `bin_main_wiring_reg_test`.

## Secrets-never-logged

Refresh tokens: never printed by the export (`--check` or not — asserted per test), never persisted by the queue lane, never in mint-failure messages. The action keeps the refresh token in a step env var and writes only the minted access token to `$GITHUB_ENV`. Redaction layers unchanged and upstream of every new surface.
