AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),

  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'

AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'

+/// Headless `fa provider export <name> [--check]` (issue #1704): mints a
+/// fresh Bearer credential for the saved ChatGPT/Codex login and prints the
+/// shell lines external tools eval — the `GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)`
+/// parity for the Codex backend.
+///
+/// The full OAuth blob lives in the entry's secure-store slot; the export
+/// refreshes it when stale (so the minted access token is fresh, not the
+/// possibly-expired stored one) and prints ONLY the access token — the
+/// refresh token never leaves the store. `--check` reports credential
+/// health without printing any secret. The base URL is always the Codex
+/// backend: ChatGPT access tokens are accepted ONLY by
+/// `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/...`, never by api.openai.com.
+library;
+
+import '../exceptions.dart';
+import '../model_roles/provider_catalog.dart' show resolveCliProviderSpec;
+import '../providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart';
+import 'agent_cli.dart';
+import 'cli_args.dart';
+import 'custom_providers.dart';
+
+/// The exported base URL: the one endpoint family these tokens serve.
+const chatGptExportBaseUrl = chatGptCodexBaseUrl;
+
+/// The shell lines an external tool evals: `export OPENAI_API_KEY=<fresh>`
+/// + `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=<codex backend>`.
+String chatGptExportLines({required String accessToken}) =>
+    'export OPENAI_API_KEY=$accessToken\n'
+    'export OPENAI_BASE_URL=$chatGptExportBaseUrl';
+
+/// The `--check` health lines for [credentials]: expiry state and
+/// refreshability, never a token value. The SSO caveat is part of the
+/// contract (issue #1704 notes): corporate session policies can shorten
+/// lifetimes or revoke refresh tokens, so the check says exactly that.
+List<String> chatGptExportCheckLines(
+  ChatGptOAuthCredentials credentials,
+  String name,
+  DateTime now,
+) {
+  final expiresAt = credentials.expiresAt;
+  final expiry = expiresAt == null
+      ? 'access token expiry unknown'
+      : expiresAt.isBefore(now)
+      ? 'access token EXPIRED'
+      : 'access token expires in ${expiresAt.difference(now).inMinutes} min';
+  return [
+    // The decode contract guarantees a non-empty refresh token, so a
+    // stored login is always refreshable HERE — the risk is revocation.
+    '$name: $expiry; refresh token present (refreshable)',
+    'note: corporate/SSO session policies can shorten lifetimes or revoke '
+        'refresh tokens at any time',
+  ];
+}

+  List<CustomProviderEntry> entries,
+  String name,
+) {
+  final spec = resolveCliProviderSpec(name);
+  if (spec?.kind == 'chatgpt-codex') {
+    // The kind itself (`chatgpt` / `chatgpt-codex`): the saved entry is
+    // located by its apiType, first match.
+    for (final entry in entries) {
+      if (resolveCliProviderSpec(entry.apiType)?.kind == 'chatgpt-codex') {
+        return entry;
+      }
+    }
+    return null;
+  }
+  final entry = CustomProviderRegistry(entries).find(name);
+  if (entry == null) return null;
+  return resolveCliProviderSpec(entry.apiType)?.kind == 'chatgpt-codex'
+      ? entry
+      : null;

AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),

  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'

Then stack is non-empty → the DEFAULT slot wins over refreshTokenEnv. Is that intended? That describes refreshTokenEnv (2) BEFORE default slot (3). The implementation checks stack.isEmpty first (which includes the default slot) and only falls to mint when the stack is empty. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'

Now I have the full providers_queue_runtime.dart. Several observations:

**Observation A (potential correctness issue):** In `buildProviderQueueChain`, the refreshTokenEnv-only entry: `ApiKeyRing(baseName: keyEnv, credentials: [ApiKeyCredential(refreshName, refreshValue)])`. Wait — `baseName: keyEnv` where keyEnv here = `entry.apiKeyEnv ?? chatGptOAuthCredentialsEnvName`. Hmm, but this is the "refreshTokenEnv-only entry" case — i.e., `entry.apiKeyEnv == null`. So keyEnv = CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS (the default slot name). The ring carries the refresh token credential named by refreshName. OK.

Wait, there's a subtle issue: the mint path is taken when `stack.isEmpty` — meaning `collectKeyStack(secrets, keyEnv)` is empty. But consider an entry with BOTH `apiKeyEnv` (set, resolvable) and `refreshTokenEnv` — stack non-empty → mint path skipped, apiKeyEnv used. Fine (documented ladder).

But now the interesting case: entry with `refreshTokenEnv` AND no `apiKeyEnv`, but the default slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` IS present in secrets (e.g., the user has a stored login). Then stack is non-empty → the DEFAULT slot wins over refreshTokenEnv. Is that intended? The PR description ladder says: 1. apiKeyEnv value; 2. refreshTokenEnv mints; 3. apiKeyEnv omitted → default Keychain slot resolves. The implemented ladder: apiKeyEnv → default slot (CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS) → refreshTokenEnv. So if both a stored login exists AND refreshTokenEnv is set, the stored login wins and the refresh env is silently ignored. Hmm. Is that the documented order? PR says "resolve credentials on a ladder: 1. apiKeyEnv ... 2. new refreshTokenEnv field ... 3. apiKeyEnv omitted → the default Keychain slot". That describes refreshTokenEnv (2) BEFORE default slot (3). The implementation checks stack.isEmpty first (which includes the default slot) and only falls to mint when the stack is empty. So implemented precedence = apiKeyEnv > default slot > refreshTokenEnv, while documented = apiKeyEnv > refreshTokenEnv > default slot.

Wait, let me re-check. In collectQueueSecrets (startup.dart), the names list is:
``
[?entry.apiKeyEnv, ?entry.refreshTokenEnv, if (entry.apiKeyEnv == null && chatgpt) chatGptOAuthCredentialsEnvName]
``
So the secrets snapshot includes: apiKeyEnv value, refreshTokenEnv value, and the default slot.

In buildProviderQueueChain:
- `stack = collectKeyStack(secrets, keyEnv)` — keyEnv = apiKeyEnv ?? CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS. If the default slot is in secrets (e.g., the machine has a stored login in the secure store), stack is non-empty → uses default slot, NEVER mints from refreshTokenEnv even though the entry explicitly names refreshTokenEnv.

So yes: an entry that EXPLICITLY says `refreshTokenEnv: CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN` silently ignores its named refresh token when the local Keychain happens to hold a login for a DIFFERENT account (the stored-login slot). On a headless runner there's no Keychain so this is unlikely to matter... but consider a dev machine with a stored login for account A, and a queue entry with refreshTokenEnv pointing to account B's refresh token: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] queue silently uses account A's stored login. That's a real precedence mismatch vs the documented ladder (PR text: refreshTokenEnv is #2, default slot #3). This is a correctness/doc-consistency finding. Severity: IMPORTANT (or BLOCKING?). The PR's own README says: "an entry with no `apiKeyEnv` resolves the saved login's Keychain slot automatically, a `refreshTokenEnv: CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN` entry mints its initial access token on the fly". The README lists auto-slot first, mint second. Hmm, so README order matches implementation (auto-slot before mint) but the pr_info "What changed" lists mint before default slot. The ladder in pr_info.md:

"resolve credentials on a ladder:
 1. apiKeyEnv value ...
 2. new refreshTokenEnv: field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation

So per the PR description itself, refreshTokenEnv (#2) should beat the default slot (#3). The code does the opposite when both are present. Also the skip message logic: `if (stack.isEmpty && refreshValue.isEmpty)` — skip when both missing. And the mint branch is `if (stack.isEmpty)`. So mint only when default slot empty. This is a genuine behavioral divergence between the documented ladder and the implementation. I'd call it IMPORTANT (not blocking — behavior is coherent, and README/inline docs describe auto-slot before mint... actually the code comment in providers_queue_runtime.dart says: "else the entry's refreshTokenEnv ... else the default Keychain slot name" — which describes refreshTokenEnv BEFORE default slot. That's the doc-ladder in the code's own header comment: apiKeyEnv → refreshTokenEnv → default slot. The implementation contradicts its own doc comment. AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no

  on every new user

  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"

That describes refreshTokenEnv (2) BEFORE default slot (3). The implementation checks stack.isEmpty first (which includes the default slot) and only falls to mint when the stack is empty. AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,

  on every new user

  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'

AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.

  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the

  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).

  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'

Wait — `baseName: keyEnv` where keyEnv here = `entry.apiKeyEnv ?? chatGptOAuthCredentialsEnvName`. Hmm, but this is the "refreshTokenEnv-only entry" case — i.e., `entry.apiKeyEnv == null`. So keyEnv = CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS (the default slot name). The ring carries the refresh token credential named by refreshName. OK.

Wait, there's a subtle issue: the mint path is taken when `stack.isEmpty` — meaning `collectKeyStack(secrets, keyEnv)` is empty. But consider an entry with BOTH `apiKeyEnv` (set, resolvable) and `refreshTokenEnv` — stack non-empty → mint path skipped, apiKeyEnv used. Fine (documented ladder).

But now the interesting case: entry with `refreshTokenEnv` AND no `apiKeyEnv`, but the default slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` IS present in secrets (e.g., the user has a stored login). Then stack is non-empty → the DEFAULT slot wins over refreshTokenEnv. Is that intended? The PR description ladder says: 1. apiKeyEnv value; 2. refreshTokenEnv mints; 3. apiKeyEnv omitted → default Keychain slot resolves. The implemented ladder: apiKeyEnv → default slot (CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS) → refreshTokenEnv. So if both a stored login exists AND refreshTokenEnv is set, the stored login wins and the refresh env is silently ignored. Hmm. Is that the documented order? PR says "resolve credentials on a ladder: 1. apiKeyEnv ... 2. new refreshTokenEnv field ... 3. apiKeyEnv omitted → the default Keychain slot". That describes refreshTokenEnv (2) BEFORE default slot (3). The implementation checks stack.isEmpty first (which includes the default slot) and only falls to mint when the stack is empty. So implemented precedence = apiKeyEnv > default slot > refreshTokenEnv, while documented = apiKeyEnv > refreshTokenEnv > default slot.

``
So the secrets snapshot includes: apiKeyEnv value, refreshTokenEnv value, and the default slot.

- `stack = collectKeyStack(secrets, keyEnv)` — keyEnv = apiKeyEnv ?? CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS. If the default slot is in secrets (e.g., the machine has a stored login in the secure store), stack is non-empty → uses default slot, NEVER mints from refreshTokenEnv even though the entry explicitly names refreshTokenEnv.

So yes: an entry that EXPLICITLY says `refreshTokenEnv: CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN` silently ignores its named refresh token when the local Keychain happens to hold a login for a DIFFERENT account (the stored-login slot). On a headless runner there's no Keychain so this is unlikely to matter... but consider a dev machine with a stored login for account A, and a queue entry with refreshTokenEnv pointing to account B's refresh token: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] queue silently uses account A's stored login. AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'

PR says "resolve credentials on a ladder: 1. apiKeyEnv ... 2. new refreshTokenEnv field ... 3. apiKeyEnv omitted → the default Keychain slot". That describes refreshTokenEnv (2) BEFORE default slot (3). The implementation checks stack.isEmpty first (which includes the default slot) and only falls to mint when the stack is empty. AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'

2. In `tryDecodeChatGptCredentials`, the fallback path: JSON object with `access_token` → returns credentials with empty refresh/id tokens. Note that the returned `expiresAt` is null here even if the JSON has `expires_at`. Hmm, a partial object loses `expires_at`. Minor.

Wait — actually there's a subtle bug: `ChatGptOAuthCredentials.decode` for a *partial* JSON object missing `refresh_token` would throw FormatException('missing refresh_token'). Then tryDecode re-parses JSON and returns the degraded bearer. But for a JSON object that HAS refresh_token but the decode failed for another reason? Decode only fails if any of access_token/refresh_token/id_token missing or not a string, or not a Map, or invalid JSON. So if it has all three, decode succeeds. The degraded path is only for missing-field objects → OK, refresh degraded is right.

Now I have the full providers_queue_runtime.dart. Several observations:

**Observation A (potential correctness issue):** In `buildProviderQueueChain`, the refreshTokenEnv-only entry: `ApiKeyRing(baseName: keyEnv, credentials: [ApiKeyCredential(refreshName, refreshValue)])`. Wait — `baseName: keyEnv` where keyEnv here = `entry.apiKeyEnv ?? chatGptOAuthCredentialsEnvName`. Hmm, but this is the "refreshTokenEnv-only entry" case — i.e., `entry.apiKeyEnv == null`. So keyEnv = CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS (the default slot name). The ring carries the refresh token credential named by refreshName. OK.

Wait, there's a subtle issue: the mint path is taken when `stack.isEmpty` — meaning `collectKeyStack(secrets, keyEnv)` is empty. But consider an entry with BOTH `apiKeyEnv` (set, resolvable) and `refreshTokenEnv` — stack non-empty → mint path skipped, apiKeyEnv used. Fine (documented ladder).

But now the interesting case: entry with `refreshTokenEnv` AND no `apiKeyEnv`, but the default slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` IS present in secrets (e.g., the user has a stored login). Then stack is non-empty → the DEFAULT slot wins over refreshTokenEnv. Is that intended? The PR description ladder says: 1. apiKeyEnv value; 2. refreshTokenEnv mints; 3. apiKeyEnv omitted → default Keychain slot resolves. The implemented ladder: apiKeyEnv → default slot (CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS) → refreshTokenEnv. So if both a stored login exists AND refreshTokenEnv is set, the stored login wins and the refresh env is silently ignored. Hmm. Is that the documented order? PR says "resolve credentials on a ladder: 1. apiKeyEnv ... 2. new refreshTokenEnv field ... 3. apiKeyEnv omitted → the default Keychain slot". That describes refreshTokenEnv (2) BEFORE default slot (3). The implementation checks stack.isEmpty first (which includes the default slot) and only falls to mint when the stack is empty. So implemented precedence = apiKeyEnv > default slot > refreshTokenEnv, while documented = apiKeyEnv > refreshTokenEnv > default slot.

``
[?entry.apiKeyEnv, ?entry.refreshTokenEnv, if (entry.apiKeyEnv == null && chatgpt) chatGptOAuthCredentialsEnvName]

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'

Now I have the full providers_queue_runtime.dart. Several observations:

**Observation A (potential correctness issue):** In `buildProviderQueueChain`, the refreshTokenEnv-only entry: `ApiKeyRing(baseName: keyEnv, credentials: [ApiKeyCredential(refreshName, refreshValue)])`. Wait — `baseName: keyEnv` where keyEnv here = `entry.apiKeyEnv ?? chatGptOAuthCredentialsEnvName`. Hmm, but this is the "refreshTokenEnv-only entry" case — i.e., `entry.apiKeyEnv == null`. So keyEnv = CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS (the default slot name). The ring carries the refresh token credential named by refreshName. OK.

Wait, there's a subtle issue: the mint path is taken when `stack.isEmpty` — meaning `collectKeyStack(secrets, keyEnv)` is empty. But consider an entry with BOTH `apiKeyEnv` (set, resolvable) and `refreshTokenEnv` — stack non-empty → mint path skipped, apiKeyEnv used. Fine (documented ladder).

But now the interesting case: entry with `refreshTokenEnv` AND no `apiKeyEnv`, but the default slot `CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS` IS present in secrets (e.g., the user has a stored login). Then stack is non-empty → the DEFAULT slot wins over refreshTokenEnv. Is that intended? The PR description ladder says: 1. apiKeyEnv value; 2. refreshTokenEnv mints; 3. apiKeyEnv omitted → default Keychain slot resolves. The implemented ladder: apiKeyEnv → default slot (CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS) → refreshTokenEnv. So if both a stored login exists AND refreshTokenEnv is set, the stored login wins and the refresh env is silently ignored. Hmm. Is that the documented order? PR says "resolve credentials on a ladder: 1. apiKeyEnv ... 2. new refreshTokenEnv field ... 3. apiKeyEnv omitted → the default Keychain slot". That describes refreshTokenEnv (2) BEFORE default slot (3). The implementation checks stack.isEmpty first (which includes the default slot) and only falls to mint when the stack is empty. So implemented precedence = apiKeyEnv > default slot > refreshTokenEnv, while documented = apiKeyEnv > refreshTokenEnv > default slot.

Wait, let me re-check. In collectQueueSecrets (startup.dart), the names list is:
``
[?entry.apiKeyEnv, ?entry.refreshTokenEnv, if (entry.apiKeyEnv == null && chatgpt) chatGptOAuthCredentialsEnvName]
``
So the secrets snapshot includes: apiKeyEnv value, refreshTokenEnv value, and the default slot.

In buildProviderQueueChain:
- `stack = collectKeyStack(secrets, keyEnv)` — keyEnv = apiKeyEnv ?? CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS. If the default slot is in secrets (e.g., the machine has a stored login in the secure store), stack is non-empty → uses default slot, NEVER mints from refreshTokenEnv even though the entry explicitly names refreshTokenEnv.

So yes: an entry that EXPLICITLY says `refreshTokenEnv: CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN` silently ignores its named refresh token when the local Keychain happens to hold a login for a DIFFERENT account (the stored-login slot). On a headless runner there's no Keychain so this is unlikely to matter... but consider a dev machine with a stored login for account A, and a queue entry with refreshTokenEnv pointing to account B's refresh token: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] queue silently uses account A's stored login. That's a real precedence mismatch vs the documented ladder (PR text: refreshTokenEnv is #2, default slot #3). This is a correctness/doc-consistency finding. Severity: IMPORTANT (or BLOCKING?). The PR's own README says: "an entry with no `apiKeyEnv` resolves the saved login's Keychain slot automatically, a `refreshTokenEnv: CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN` entry mints its initial access token on the fly". The README lists auto-slot first, mint second. Hmm, so README order matches implementation (auto-slot before mint) but the pr_info "What changed" lists mint before default slot. The ladder in pr_info.md:

"resolve credentials on a ladder:
 1. apiKeyEnv value ...
 2. new refreshTokenEnv: field — the entry's stream mints the initial access token on FIRST activation
 3. apiKeyEnv omitted → the default Keychain slot CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS resolves env→secure-store like every other queue name"

So per the PR description itself, refreshTokenEnv (#2) should beat the default slot (#3). The code does the opposite when both are present. Also the skip message logic: `if (stack.isEmpty && refreshValue.isEmpty)` — skip when both missing. And the mint branch is `if (stack.isEmpty)`. So mint only when default slot empty. This is a genuine behavioral divergence between the documented ladder and the implementation. I'd call it IMPORTANT (not blocking — behavior is coherent, and README/inline docs describe auto-slot before mint... actually the code comment in providers_queue_runtime.dart says: "else the entry's refreshTokenEnv ... else the default Keychain slot name" — which describes refreshTokenEnv BEFORE default slot. That's the doc-ladder in the code's own header comment: apiKeyEnv → refreshTokenEnv → default slot. The implementation contradicts its own doc comment. That's a solid IMPORTANT finding (doc/behavior mismatch that changes which account serves traffic).

Let me double check the header comment:

**Observation B:** `_mintingStreamForKey` — memoized `minted` Future. If the mint fails, `minted` keeps the failed future; every subsequent call awaits the same failed future → each activation surfaces a terminal error event → queue advances. That's arguably fine (fail fast; a retry would need a rebuild). But note: on failure the memoized failed future persists — the entry never retries minting for the runtime's lifetime. name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'

name: 'ChatGPT Codex auth'
description: >-
  Mint a fresh ChatGPT/Codex access token from a stored refresh token
  (issue #1704). Exports OPENAI_API_KEY (the fresh Bearer) and
  OPENAI_BASE_URL (the Codex backend — these tokens serve ONLY
  chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, never api.openai.com) for downstream
  steps. invalid_grant / revoked refresh tokens fail the job fast and
  loudly — a bench pipeline must never park on a dead credential.

# Direct curl against auth.openai.com — the same issuer + client id fa's
# own OAuth uses (lib/src/providers/chatgpt_oauth.dart). No third-party
# action; the refresh token arrives only through the `refresh-token` input.
inputs:
  refresh-token:
    [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] 'ChatGPT OAuth refresh token (offline_access grant)'
    required: true
  base-url:
    description: 'Codex backend base URL to export'
    required: false
    default: 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.refresh-token }}
        CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.base-url }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        client_id='app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann'
        body_file="$(mktemp)"
        trap 'rm -f "$body_file"' EXIT
        http_code=$(curl -sS -o "$body_file" -w '%{http_code}' \
          https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d "{\"grant_type\":\"refresh_token\",\"refresh_token\":\"$CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN\",\"client_id\":\"$client_id\"}") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token endpoint unreachable (curl failed) — check runner network/egress'
          exit 1
        }
        error=$(jq -r '.error // empty' "$body_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ "$http_code" != "200" ]; then
          if [ "$error" = "invalid_grant" ] || [ "$error" = "invalid_request" ]; then
            echo '::error::ChatGPT refresh token rejected (error='"$error"') — the stored refresh token is expired or revoked. Re-authenticate once with `fa /provider chatgpt oauth` (or `codex login`), then update the CHATGPT_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. SSO/corporate session policies can revoke refresh tokens at any time.'
          else
            echo '::error::ChatGPT token refresh failed (HTTP '"$http_code"'): '"$(cat "$body_file")"
          fi
          exit 1
        fi
        access_token=$(jq -er '.access_token // empty' "$body_file") || {
          echo '::error::ChatGPT token response carried no access_token'
          exit 1
        }
        {
          echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=$access_token"
          echo "OPENAI_BASE_URL=$CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        echo 'ChatGPT Codex credential minted: OPENAI_API_KEY + OPENAI_BASE_URL exported (account quotas are per-account; a 401/403 in a bench step means the window is exhausted or the token was revoked — fail fast, never park).'
